solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: See what is being said? (3-4)

blocks.note: the surface wants 'understand', as in 'I see'; the setter means using your eyes
the words spoken, which here are watched rather than heard

annotation.walkthrough: 'See what is being said?' sounds like 'do you understand?', but taken literally it describes reading words off someone's lips.
annotation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to follow speech by watching the speaker's mouth, literally seeing the words.

entries.clue: Animal catcher employed by professional association (5)

indicatorNotes.employed by: the answer is at work inside the following words

annotation.surface: A trade body takes on someone to round up stray animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Employed by' reads as a job offer, but it means the answer sits inside the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used to catch cattle and horses.

entries.clue: Great office of strait-laced English clergyman (5,8)

annotation.surface: A stuffy English vicar holds some grand position in the church.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain the prime minister's post is one of the four Great Offices of State, alongside Chancellor, Foreign Secretary and Home Secretary.
annotation.definitionFit: Prime minister is the highest of the Great Offices of State in British government.

entries.clue: Additional cast member having little to do (5)

annotation.definition2: cast member having little to do

blocks.note: more than the usual amount, over and above

blocks.clueFragment: cast member having little to do
blocks.note: a background performer in a film crowd scene, with no lines

annotation.surface: A spare actor is hired who has hardly any part.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses run together so smoothly that the clue reads as one description of a bit-part player.
annotation.definitionFit: An extra is something additional, and also a background performer in a film.

entries.clue: Stubborn person put on small island (6)

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
a key (or cay) is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys

annotation.surface: An obstinate man gets marooned on a tiny island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like 'marooned', but it means dressing: DON.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative use: the animal is proverbially obstinate, so the name is thrown at a mulish human.

entries.clue: Bring back drink fit for a king (5)

indicatorNotes.Bring back: bringing the word back reads it right to left

annotation.surface: Someone asks for a drink to be brought back that would suit royalty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bring back drink' reads like ordering another round, but it tells you to write LAGER backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a king.

entries.clue: Refuse to criticise (7)

blocks.note: the noun, stressed REF-use: household waste
a British verb for dismissing something as worthless

annotation.surface: Someone declines to find fault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' wants to be the verb, declining; it is the noun, household waste.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the noun for waste, a plain synonym of the noun refuse, and the informal British verb meaning to pour scorn on.

entries.clue: Pleasure beginning to gain approval (13)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of 'gain' is its first letter

annotation.surface: The joy of starting to win people's backing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to gain approval' reads as one phrase about winning support; split it after 'gain' to find G and the formal word for approval.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names the satisfaction felt when a wish is met, which is a kind of pleasure.

entries.clue: Boisterous young woman jetted all over naked (7)

indicatorNotes.naked: stripped of its outer covering, the phrase loses its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.over: the letters are turned over into a new order

blocks.note: JETTEDALL without its outer letters J and L

annotation.surface: A rowdy girl has flown all over the world without her clothes on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All over' looks like a single phrase meaning everywhere; 'all' is fodder and 'over' is the mixing instruction. A ladette is British slang for a young woman who drinks and behaves as rowdily as the lads.
annotation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves in a loud, hard-drinking, laddish way.

entries.clue: What goes round room, bypassing senior management? (8,5)

blocks.note: the strip of wood running round the base of a room's walls

annotation.surface: Office gossip that circulates while the bosses are kept out of the loop.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: read the answer as a verb phrase, going around the company board. A skirting board is the wooden strip where wall meets floor.
annotation.definitionFit: A skirting board runs round the bottom of a room's walls.

entries.clue: Work with case in theatre (7)

indicatorNotes.case in: a case is an outer shell, so the case in a word is its first and last letters

blocks.note: opera is Latin for 'works', and an opera is a musical work

annotation.surface: A surgeon deals with a patient in the operating theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces. In hospital talk a case is a patient and the theatre is where surgery happens.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes a surgeon at work on a patient in the operating theatre, which is exactly what operating means.

entries.clue: Papers I returned to fool (5)

indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so read right to left

annotation.surface: Someone sent the documents back to a clown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returned to' reads as sending papers back to someone; it is TO that comes back.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a stupid person, and both work as insults.

entries.clue: In GCHQ, briefly shed light on computer problem (6)

indicatorNotes.In: one piece goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: GCHQ losing its last letter Q

annotation.surface: Inside Britain's spy agency, someone briefly explains a bug in the system.
annotation.walkthrough: LIT goes inside G_CH. GCHQ is Britain's government communications and signals intelligence agency.
annotation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden malfunction, especially in a computer.

entries.clue: Broadcast enraged eminent individual (7)

indicatorNotes.Broadcast: scattered, like seed sown by hand

annotation.surface: A furious bigwig goes on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a TV or radio verb, but its older sense is scattering seed, which is why it mixes letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank or eminence, originally a Spanish nobleman.

entries.clue: Calm surrounds every other part of unitary authority (7)

indicatorNotes.surrounds: one word goes round the other
indicatorNotes.every other part of: every other means one in two, so only alternate letters of the next word are kept, here the second, fourth and sixth

annotation.surface: Peace settles across a local council area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unitary authority' looks like a single term, a type of English local council; split it, and 'authority' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having authority over people means having the power to direct them.

entries.clue: Exquisite selection (6)

blocks.note: an adjective: of the finest quality, as a butcher's best cuts
a noun: the range to pick from, or the pick made

annotation.surface: A superb range on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: One word is the adjective, the other the noun, and both are CHOICE.
annotation.definitionFit: Choice means of very good quality, and also a selection.

entries.clue: Greek character stops behind raised weapon (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: plugs a gap, so it sits inside
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifted up means read bottom to top

annotation.surface: A Greek hero halts after lifting his sword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a figure from Greek myth; it is a letter of the alphabet. 'Stops' is the verb for plugging a hole, as with a stopper.
annotation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword.

entries.clue: Strange article about invention (5)

blocks.note: a lie is an invention, a made-up story

annotation.surface: An odd piece of writing concerning a new gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a newspaper piece and 'invention' as a gadget; they are AN and LIE. A(LIE)N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: something foreign to your experience feels strange.

entries.clue: Successor man announced in letter? (7)

indicatorNotes.announced: said out loud, so the sound counts

blocks.note: an heir is a successor, male = man

annotation.surface: A letter announces who will inherit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that airmail is one kind of letter, not a synonym for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a letter flown overseas is sent by this service.
annotation.definitionNote: airmail is a way of sending a letter, so the question mark marks the definition by example

entries.clue: Genuine monarch’s principal possession? (5)

indicatorNotes.principal: the chief letter of a word is its first

annotation.surface: A king's most prized true possession.
annotation.walkthrough: A monarch's chief possession is the kingdom itself, which is why 'possession' gets a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory a monarch holds.

entries.clue: Cut into network cable at both ends (5)

indicatorNotes.at both ends: take just the first and last letters

annotation.surface: An engineer slices into network cabling at each end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut into' is a verb and the definition, not a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: To lance is to cut into, as a surgeon lances a boil.

entries.clue: Judgement voided debatable conclusion (13)

indicatorNotes.voided: emptied, so only the outer letters remain

annotation.surface: A ruling has thrown out a contested finding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Voided' sounds legal, like a judgement being overturned; it means emptying a word.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: a court's formal decision on a disputed point is called this, the same as its judgement.

entries.clue: Sign up loner to go travelling (5)

indicatorNotes.to go travelling: the letters set off and move around

annotation.surface: A solitary type joins a group tour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' belongs to the definition, sign up, not a reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting your name down for a course or club, the British spelling with one L.

entries.clue: Fantastic story can spread in capital city (7)

indicatorNotes.spread: the letters are spread out and rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: placed in the next word, so it sits between that word's letters

annotation.surface: A tall tale that a tin can was smeared around the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, as in 'the story can spread'; it is the noun, a tin, supplying three letters to mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A romance is a fanciful tale of adventure, originally a medieval tale of chivalry.
